children: Asian currencies are mixed against the dollar, as investors are focusing on the U.S. midterm elections. The first polls are closing, with control of Congress at stake. Democrats are likely to take control of the House and Senate, say ANZ Research analysts in a note. This would constrain the Trump administration's policy agenda and likely lead to gridlock on key issues, they add. The U.S. dollar is 0.1% lower at 158.49 yen, while the Australian dollar is flat at US$0.6967, LSEG data show.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
